text.p: BLANTYRE, Jan 30 (Reuter) These are the leading stories in the Malawi Press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former Zambian President Kenneth Kaunda silently entered Malawi on Wednesday and held discussions in camera with President Bakili Muluzi in Lilongwe, the administrative capital. - The High Court in Lilongwe increased rape and robbery sentences from to seven and five years respectively, from three years, two days after Judicial Commission chairman Duncan Tambala accused the lower magistrate court of excessive leniency.

- Commerce and Industry Minister Chakakala Chaziya was at a loss on Wednesday to explain which regional grouping Malawi would belong to after SADC was quoted as saying its members should not hold dual-membership with COMESA.
- Thieves on Tuesday broke into the home of President Bakili Muluzi's guard commander at the presidential palace, police sources said.
- Beleagured COMESA Secretary General Bingu wa Mutharika arrived in Malawi at the weekend and was on Wednesday scheduled to meet President Bakili Muluzi in Lilongwe.
